title: Chapter 16: Don’t Spend Your Night Here
html:
“I’m getting ahead of myself. The landlord is suspicious, but that doesn’t make him the murderer.” Chen Ge scratched his head. “I should talk to some of the other tenants and see what they know.”

Since arriving, Chen Ge had encountered four people: the woman hiding behind her door, Wang Qi with his missing-person notices, the irritable landlord, and the elderly man in the wheelchair.

“The old man lives with the landlord, so talking to him is out. The woman downstairs gives me the creeps. That leaves Wang Qi. He should know something about this place.” Chen Ge left the thermos in his room, locked the door behind him, and headed downstairs.

The motion-activated light flickered on, revealing Wang Qi walking along the corridor with his stack of notices. He slipped one beneath every door, whether the room appeared occupied or not. That immediately struck Chen Ge as strange. Missing-person notices were normally posted in busy public places, yet Wang Qi was concentrating on this nearly deserted apartment building.

Chen Ge followed quietly. Only after Wang Qi pushed the final notice beneath a door did he speak. “Brother, I know what it’s like to have someone you love disappear, but you need to take care of yourself. Doing this over and over is only punishing you.”

At the sound of Chen Ge’s voice, Wang Qi slowly turned. His clouded eyes never seemed to settle on a single point. “Understand? None of you could ever understand how I feel. And I never asked you to.”

Chen Ge did not argue. Instead, he took out his phone and pulled up the missing-person report filed after his parents vanished. “I’m not pretending. My parents disappeared without warning half a year ago. At first, I was devastated too.”

Wang Qi stared at the image on the phone for a long time before saying, “I sympathize with you, but our situations are different. My fiancée is coming back. I can feel that she hasn’t gone far.”

“Would you tell me what happened? We’re in similar situations. Maybe I can help,” Chen Ge said. To his own surprise, he genuinely meant it.

Wang Qi hesitated. Perhaps remembering that Chen Ge had helped him pick up the notice earlier, his expression softened. “Thank you, but you can’t help me. You seem like a good person, so take my advice: leave while you still can. Don’t spend the night here.”

“I’ve already paid. You’ll need a better reason than that if you want me to leave.” Chen Ge had come to complete the Trial Mission. Giving up would mean losing his chance to unlock Murder by Midnight forever.

“Which matters more, your life or your money?” Wang Qi glanced around to make sure no one was watching, then lowered his voice. “Everyone here knows people were murdered in this building years ago.”

“I’ve heard rumors, but I couldn’t find anything about them online. I assumed they were just stories,” Chen Ge replied.

“This place used to be called Fu An Apartments. After the incident, the name was changed to Ping An Apartments. The murders were major news at the time, and they were never solved. People say the dead never found peace, so their spirits return to the place where they died every night at midnight.” Wang Qi sounded as though he believed every word.

“You still believe stories like that?” Chen Ge gave an awkward smile. Inside, however, he was extremely tense. After everything he had seen, he knew better than most that the supernatural could be real, and he had no desire to encounter another spirit tonight.

“I didn’t believe them either—not until my fiancée disappeared near this place.” Wang Qi dragged a hand through his hair, his exhaustion obvious.

“Why did your fiancée come somewhere like this in the first place?” Chen Ge asked. Her disappearance sounded strangely similar to what had happened to his parents.

“Honestly, I don’t know. I had never even heard of this apartment building before she disappeared. I learned the name from the police; they told me this was the last place connected to any useful lead.” Wang Qi let his hands fall. “I ran out of other ideas. That’s why I moved in.”

“Then, have you discovered anything?”

Wang Qi parted his lips, then stopped before saying anything. Instead, he pulled out his phone and typed a message.

“My fiancée was kidnapped by the people living here!”

Chen Ge stared at the message, stunned by the sudden turn. “Brother, kidnapping and disappearance are two very different things.”

Wang Qi motioned sharply for him to be quiet. Turning his back to the corridor, he held out his phone so Chen Ge could see the inbox. As Chen Ge read the screen, his eyes widened.

There was a message from Wang Qi’s missing fiancée.

The message contained only two words—‘Save me!’ What made it truly unsettling was the timestamp: 2:00 a.m. the previous night.

“Your missing fiancée sent you a message in the middle of the night?” After the initial shock, Chen Ge quickly recovered. “Why didn’t you take this to the police? If the message is real, it could mean she’s alive.”

“You might not believe me, but I receive the same message from her every night after midnight. The problem is that whenever I finally fall asleep, the message disappears as though it never existed.” Wang Qi pointed to his exhausted eyes. “I’ve been afraid to sleep because I don’t want to lose it again.”

“The message disappears when you sleep?” Chen Ge had never heard of anything like it.

“I know you think I’m crazy, but everything I’m telling you is true.” Wang Qi leaned against the wall for support and pocketed his phone. “Other impossible things have happened too. My fiancée’s belongings sometimes appear in my room without warning. It feels as though she’s trying to remind me to keep looking for her.”

At that last sentence, Chen Ge’s eyelids twitched. After everything he had experienced over the previous few days, he could not dismiss the possibility that something supernatural had happened to Wang Qi’s fiancée. If Wang Qi was telling the truth, she might be trying to contact him somehow.

“My fiancée disappeared near this building, and this place has changed my entire life. Listen to me—it’s cursed. People who stay too close to it end up suffering. Leave while you still can.” Wang Qi seemed unused to speaking for so long; by the end, his face had gone pale with exhaustion.
